title: Music, Sweat & Volume
description: A full music and fitness deep dive — 90s grunge anthems, songs everyone screams along to, gym culture classics, legendary rock tracks, 90s alternative icons, and the ultimate pump-up jams.

questions.question: This Seattle grunge band's 1994 hit 'Black Hole Sun' — featuring a hypnotic guitar riff and a surreal music video of smiling faces melting in the sun — became one of the defining songs of the era, fronted by the powerhouse vocals of Chris Cornell.

Written by guitarist Jerry Cantrell about his father's harrowing Vietnam War experience, 'Rooster' was the emotional centerpiece of this Seattle band's 1992 album 'Dirt' — widely considered one of the darkest and greatest records in grunge history.

After the death of his Nirvana bandmate in 1994, drummer Dave Grohl channeled his grief by forming this rock group — largely recording their self-titled debut album alone in the studio — before building them into one of the world's biggest arena rock bands.

Fronted by charismatic vocalist Scott Weiland, this San Diego band's debut album 'Core' went multi-platinum in 1992 — powered by the Grammy-winning single 'Plush' — despite critics unfairly dismissing them as a Seattle grunge copycat from Southern California.
questions.answer: Who are the Stone Temple Pilots?

questions.question: British frontman Gavin Rossdale led this group to enormous US success in the mid-1990s with albums 'Sixteen Stone' and 'Razorblade Suitcase' — producing grunge-inflected anthems like 'Glycerine' and 'Machinehead' despite hailing from London rather than Seattle.

With its iconic piano intro and power-ballad chorus about a small-town girl and a city boy, this 1981 Journey anthem is one of the best-selling digital singles of all time — and is still screamed by crowds at arenas, stadiums, and karaoke bars worldwide.

Neil Diamond's 1969 pop classic has become the world's greatest call-and-response anthem — with crowds worldwide erupting in 'BA BA BA!' between chorus lines — and is an official tradition at Boston Red Sox home games at Fenway Park.

This 2003 debut single from Las Vegas rockers The Killers — with its breathless, jealous lyrics about watching a lover with someone else — became one of the longest-charting songs in UK singles history, reappearing on the charts every single summer for over a decade.

Written by Noel Gallagher and sung by his brother Liam, this 1995 Oasis acoustic anthem became the first song every beginner guitarist learns — and is widely regarded as the most overplayed campfire and open-mic staple of the past thirty years.

Composed by Jim Steinman, Bonnie Tyler's 1983 operatic power ballad builds to a theatrical climax with the repeated, desperate plea 'Turn around, bright eyes' — earning its permanent place as the quintessential karaoke anthem performed with maximum drama in bars worldwide.
questions.answer: What is 'Total Eclipse of the Heart'?

questions.question: This Hollywood actress and political activist became the unexpected queen of home fitness when her 1982 workout VHS sparked a living-room aerobics revolution — eventually selling over 17 million copies and inspiring a fitness empire of follow-up tapes.

Beachbody trainer Tony Horton designed this intense 90-day home workout program in 2004, built around the concept of 'muscle confusion' to prevent plateaus — and is fondly remembered for its motivating mantra: 'Do your best, and forget the rest.'

Colombian choreographer Alberto Perez accidentally invented this dance-fitness phenomenon in the 1990s when he forgot his aerobics music and improvised with a Latin dance cassette instead — eventually expanding it into a global craze practiced in over 180 countries.

A German fitness innovator who emigrated to New York City originally called his core-strengthening method 'Contrology' — teaching it to dancers and rehabilitation patients from the 1920s onward — until it became a global studio exercise program named after its creator.

Founded in 2012, this home fitness company turned the stationary spin bike into a live-streamed subscription class experience — and saw explosive membership growth when global gym closures during the pandemic made sweating at home suddenly very necessary.

This 1986 Bon Jovi arena anthem follows Tommy and Gina — a working-class couple struggling to make ends meet — and features a dramatic key change into a soaring chorus that virtually every human being in earshot will instinctively sing along to at full volume.

Featuring a delicate acoustic guitar intro that slowly builds to a thunderous electric climax, this 1971 Led Zeppelin epic has been voted the greatest rock song of all time by countless polls — and its famous opening notes are banned by unwritten law at guitar shops worldwide.

Joe Elliott's over-the-top vocals power this 1987 Def Leppard glam metal anthem from their record-breaking 'Hysteria' album — a song so gloriously excessive it became both a beloved classic and a reliable punchline at the same time.
questions.answer: What is 'Pour Some Sugar on Me'?

questions.question: Guitarist Slash originally played the iconic opening riff of this 1987 Guns N' Roses ballad as a throwaway warm-up exercise — calling it a silly little circus melody — before frontman Axl Rose built a love song around it that became the band's only US number-one hit.

Don Felder's 12-string guitar opens this 1977 Eagles classic, which won the Grammy for Record of the Year and features one of rock's most quoted closing lines — 'You can check out any time you like, but you can never leave' — followed by one of rock's most famous dual guitar outros.

Fronted by the bespectacled Rivers Cuomo, this LA band's 1994 debut single 'Buddy Holly' came with a Spike Jonze-directed video cleverly set on the 'Happy Days' TV show — launching a cult-beloved alternative rock career that still resonates with devoted fans decades later.

This Long Beach trio fronted by Bradley Nowell blended reggae, punk, and ska into massive party anthems like 'What I Got' and 'Santeria' — but Nowell tragically died of a heroin overdose just two months before their self-titled 1996 album became a massive posthumous hit.

This Los Angeles artist's 1994 lo-fi debut hit — opening with the self-deprecating Spanish line 'Soy un perdedor,' meaning 'I'm a loser' — became a Gen X slacker anthem, launching a shapeshifting career that bounced between hip-hop, folk, electronica, and pop.

This Oxford band's 1992 debut single — featuring a chorus about longing for a 'perfect body' and a 'perfect soul' — became an international anthem for social outsiders everywhere, though the band notoriously refused to play it live for years due to how much they disliked the song.

Formed in Los Angeles in 1983, this funk-rock powerhouse released the melancholic 'Under the Bridge' in 1992 before their 1999 album 'Californication' — featuring the Grammy-winning 'Scar Tissue' — proved they could balance raw arena energy with introspective songwriting.
questions.answer: Who are the Red Hot Chili Peppers?

questions.question: Survivor wrote this thumping 1982 guitar anthem specifically at Sylvester Stallone's request for 'Rocky III' — and its relentless opening riff has since become the world's universal pump-up song for sports montages, training sequences, and anyone about to do something epic.

In this 1984 Van Halen track, the band's legendary guitar hero Eddie Van Halen surprised rock fans by building the entire hook around a synthesizer keyboard riff — and the result became the band's first and only US number-one single.

When the horn blasts and bass drops in this 1992 House of Pain hip-hop banger, the instruction in the title becomes physically irresistible — and no stadium embodies this better than the University of Wisconsin, which plays it during every home football game.

The four-note opening of this 2003 White Stripes track — played by Jack White on guitar through an octave pedal to mimic a bass — became one of the most universally chanted riffs in sports stadium history, echoing at soccer matches, hockey arenas, and concerts worldwide.

The menacing opening riff of this heavy metal track — the lead single off Metallica's landmark 1991 'Black Album' — became legendary in baseball when New York Yankees closer Mariano Rivera used it as his entrance music throughout his entire Hall of Fame career.
